text:
Nina: Heads-up: seeing a low-rate 401 on Android when clients use HTTP/2. Small repro: two logged-in accounts sending concurrent profile requests; ~1% of A's requests come back 401 while B succeeds.
Sam: Do you have logs or a minimal repro? Could be token refresh races.
Nina: Repro pushed to internal repo (private). Curl with --http2 reproduces; forcing http/1.1 resolves it.
Oleg: Likely connection multiplexing/coalescing. OkHttp may reuse an h2 connection across origins if TLS permits; if an edge or proxy binds sessions to the connection or caches headers, a stream could get the wrong auth context.
Priya: Are we injecting Authorization in an application interceptor? That can be captured before OkHttp picks a connection.
Nina: Yes. Switched to a network interceptor and the repro vanished in local tests.
Sam: Network interceptor runs at the network layer and sees the final request, so that fits. Also ensure your Authenticator that handles 401 performs a single-threaded refresh (synchronized) and updates token storage atomically.
Oleg: Alternative mitigation: add Connection: close for suspected endpoints, but that hurts perf. Better: opt-in SDK toggle to disable h2 on Android until infra fixes proxy behavior.
Priya: Note: system OkHttp bundled on some Android images behaves differently from our shaded client; emulator images can use different HTTP/2 settings. Add this to troubleshooting and test matrix.
Nina: Example network-interceptor workaround we used:
```kotlin
client.newBuilder()
  .addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
    val tok = tokenStore.current()
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $tok")
      .build()
    chain.proceed(req)
  }
  .build()
```
Sam: For SDK team action items: 1) add doc explaining app vs network interceptor behavior and recommended pattern; 2) add an Android config flag to opt-out of h2; 3) add CI test matrix (http1/http2 across API 28/31 emulators + a physical-device lane).
CI-Bot: canary build queued: sdk-0.13.0-rc1.
Oleg: I'll create a sample-app CI job that runs the repro against both protocols and fails on any interleaved 401 pattern.
Priya: I'll draft a short migration note for mobile engineers showing the network-interceptor snippet and the reasoning.
Nina: Filed follow-up to track edge/proxy root cause and plan a postmortem once infra provides logs. Thanks all :pray:
